Calculate nearest distance between two SpatVector objects

Source: R/calc_nearest_distance.R
calc_nearest_distance.Rd

Computes the minimum distance from each feature in x to the nearest feature in y using terra::nearest(). Returns x with an added column containing the nearest distance in kilometers.

Usage

calc_nearest_distance(x, y, return_geometry = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A terra::SpatVector (polygons, points, or lines).

y

A terra::SpatVector containing target features.

return_geometry

Logical. If TRUE, returns a SpatVector with geometries. If FALSE (default), returns a tibble with polygon attributes only.

...

Additional arguments passed to terra::nearest() (e.g., method, centroids, distance).

Value

Either a terra::SpatVector or a tibble::tbl_df equal to x with an added column:

  • dist_nearest_km: minimum distance to y in kilometers.

Details

If CRS differ, y is automatically reprojected to the CRS of x.

  • Distance is 0 if features intersect.

  • If CRS is geographic (lon/lat), consider using method = "haversine".

  • For projected CRS (meters), default Euclidean distance is used.

See also

terra::nearest calc_distance

Examples

adm_div <- terra::vect(system.file("extdata", "adm_div.gpkg", package = "c4e"))
survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
points <- terra::vect(survey, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

# distance from each household to the nearest division border
calc_nearest_distance(points, terra::as.lines(adm_div))
